applicable_failures: The script only matched file names (patent|infringement|markman|daubert|invalidity, and expert-related names) and never unzipped or regex-searched document text. This is a file-name filter, not the content scan the stage requires.

The 'ex' indicator is loose: 1007-00003 counted a privilege-log retention memo as expert evidence, and 1011-00003 is a trademark matter. The 'pat' filter also misses patent matters whose files are named differently, so qualifying matters can be dropped silently.

The agent's self-assessment names only five candidates, while many surfaced matters (e.g. 1045-00004, 1012-00001, 1019-00001) have no document opened. A hand-picked shortlist from name-based hits risks excluding them.
Output for 1012-00005 appears truncated at the display cap (+4771 chars), so the full per-matter list was not seen.
critique.concerns: The goal was a text-content aggregation across all matters. The script matched only file paths, so matters with unconventionally named files would be missed. Its expert indicator was noisy: it counted a retention memo, and trademark and survey-expert matters also appeared. The candidate list of five was not justified from text evidence, and the output was cut off.
critique.recommendation: Rerun a bounded text scan that extracts .docx text for every matter. Flag patent-infringement terms and expert-retention terms (expert report, engagement letter, disclosure) separately, and print one capped line per matter. Then compare the resulting list against the surfaced matters before choosing which folders to open.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.
- A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.
- A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
- Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
What successful runs did: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.
Reconsider before moving on. If the goal was not fully reached, or any failure above applies, reopen this stage now: call stage_start with stage="Scan document text with an extraction script" and a goal that says what you will fix. Otherwise call stage_start for the next stage you need.
